english.title: Registered person fail to notify relevant person of notifiable safety incident
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[service provider]_
(B)_[registered manager]_

in respect of a regulated activity, namely **(..SPECIFY ACTIVITY..), failed, as soon as reasonably practicable after becoming aware that a notifiable safety incident had occurred, to notify

(C)_[the service user]_
(D)_[a person lawfully acting on behalf of the service user who was under 16 and not competent to make a decision in relation to their care or treatment]_
(E)_[a person lawfully acting on behalf of the service user who was over 16 and who lacked capacity in relation to the matter]_

that the incident had occurred, in accordance with regulation 20(3) of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014 in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 20(2)(a) and (3), 22(1)(d) and 23(5) of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
being the registered person in respect of a registered activity
failed, as soon as reasonably practicable after becoming aware that a notifiable safety incident had occurred
to notify the relevant person that the incident had occurred, in accordance with regulation 20(3)

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 8(1) and (2) provides that a registered person must comply with regulations 9 to 20A in carrying on a regulated activity, unless the thing to be done has by another registered person in relation to the regulated activity concerned.
(ii) As per regulation 22(4), it is a defence for a registered person to prove that they took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to prevent the breach.
